name: Damage Wrestling Federation Saturday Night Fever

date.source: The broadcast's own text ("welcome to the Opening night Damage Wrestling Federation") and its Usenet posting date.

evidence.source: The federation's own broadcast script, subject "Damage Federation <Saturday Night Fever card>" (16 July 1997)
evidence.note: The promotion's own opening-night card: two singles matches, called by Steve Williams and Terry Branch.

matches.note: Jeff Jacobs pinned Tom E. Gunn with the "Lights Out" finisher to open Damage Wrestling Federation's first-ever card. The World Championship was not on the line.
Crimson Mask pinned 100 Proof with the "Crimson Rush" after an unnamed masked man struck Proof with a steel chair behind the referee's back.

appearances.source: the broadcast's own commentary, served at /promotions/damage-1997/archive/damage-saturday-night-fever-1997-07-16.html
the broadcast's own commentary, served at /promotions/damage-1997/archive/damage-saturday-night-fever-1997-07-16.html

notes: The promotion's own opening-night card; Tom E. Gunn is already billed the World Champion by the fed's very next show despite losing his own match here, since the title was not at stake.

name: Blood Bash '97

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline ("07/19/97") and its Usenet posting date.

evidence.source: The federation's own broadcast script, subject "BLOOD BASH '97" (19 July 1997)
evidence.note: A thirteen-man, over-the-top-rope rumble billed live from the United Center in Chicago, Illinois, called by Steve Williams and Terry Branch.

eliminations.note: Lifted over the top rope after a chop exchange.
Ducked a charge and sent Morris over the top rope.
Caught in the "Glove Sleeper" and dragged over the ropes.
Put in the boston crab after a "Power Slam."
Sent out with an arm throw; the broadcast calls Crimson Mask Damage's own top-ranked wrestler.
Thrown to the ropes and out after Sychodic's own dropkick was reversed.
Eliminated together with Massive Force by a double clothesline.
Eliminated together with KC Boss by a double clothesline.
Pushed toward the ropes by Tom E. Gunn but pulled Gunn over with him; the two were eliminated in the same spot.
Pulled over the top rope by 100 Proof in the same spot that eliminated Proof.
Caught in a figure four and then the "Glove Sleeper" in the final two.

matches.note: Billed to award its winner a choice between a new Blood Bash Title and a shot at Tom E. Gunn's World Championship; General Glove chose the title shot.

appearances.source: the broadcast's own commentary, served at /promotions/damage-1997/archive/damage-blood-bash-97-1997-07-19.html
the broadcast's own commentary, served at /promotions/damage-1997/archive/damage-blood-bash-97-1997-07-19.html

notes: General Glove's own choice of a title shot over the vacant Blood Bash Title left that title unawarded in this record.

name: Damage Wrestling Federation Saturday Night Fever

date.source: The broadcast's own posting date; subject "Damage: World Championship match" (4 August 1997).

evidence.source: The federation's own broadcast script, subject "Damage: World Championship match" (4 August 1997)
evidence.note: A two-out-of-three-falls World Championship match, called by Steve Williams and Terry Branch from the Carolina Coliseum in Columbia, South Carolina.

matches.note: A two-out-of-three-falls World Championship match. Tom E. Gunn won the first fall by pinfall; General Glove won the next two, the last after a pile driver, suplex and choke slam, to take the World Championship.

appearances.source: the broadcast's own commentary, served at /promotions/damage-1997/archive/damage-world-championship-match-1997-08-04.html
the broadcast's own commentary, served at /promotions/damage-1997/archive/damage-world-championship-match-1997-08-04.html

notes: Terry Branch's own commentary names an unspecified new arrival, "The Maniac," as one reason the promotion is growing; that wrestler does not appear in this broadcast and is not minted.
